how: The Hall in the Mission is a pool parlor with eight tables and a cocktail menu, and Family Billiards is a long-running San Francisco hall with league play.
Marin Diving Center in San Rafael lists PADI Freediving among its courses, with pool sessions locally.
FPV Explorers & Racers meet weekly at Cesar Chavez Park by the Berkeley Marina to fly drones, and the Drones of San Francisco group runs FPV racing events.
Piedmont Adult School has offered beginner bagpipe courses on a practice chanter, and the Irish Pipers Band is an established San Francisco pipe band.
Lake Merced has stocked lakes with year-round fishing from docks, requiring a California license and a daily permit for the trout-stocked North Lake.
Mike's Paddle in Ballena Bay Marina runs 90-minute SUP yoga classes on calm harbor water facing the San Francisco skyline.
The San Francisco Gem and Mineral Society meets monthly at its Outer Sunset clubhouse with field trips and a fossil focus, though collecting on public land is restricted.
venue: San Francisco Gem and Mineral Society

how: The Sutro Baths ruins, Point Lobos tunnel and Fort Miley gun batteries can be explored on foot, and the Parks Conservancy has led historian walks there.
Berkeley Water Ski Club runs a slalom course at Berkeley Aquatic Park from May to September, including a Wednesday night ski league that needs no boat or membership.
Preserved in Oakland runs a two-hour beginner workshop making fresh ricotta and butter with ingredients and tools provided, and the Cheese School of SF teaches cheese-making classes.
Melody of China teaches erhu and other traditional Chinese instruments in San Francisco, and Chinese Arts & Music Center on Balboa Street sells erhus.
Jing Ying Cantonese Opera Institute, founded in Chinatown in 1997, performs and teaches Cantonese opera and runs an annual festival at the Great Star Theater.
Black Heart Tattoo at 177 Valencia St and several other Mission District studios offer custom tattoos by appointment and walk-in.
The Pacific Coast Numismatic Society (founded 1915) and the San Francisco Ancient & Foreign Coin Club hold regular meetings, the latter at the San Francisco Public Library main branch.
venue: San Francisco Ancient & Foreign Coin Club

how: Watch the Bay holds a free monthly meetup for Bay Area watch enthusiasts at Topper Jewelers in Burlingame.
Our Childhood on Columbus Avenue sells classic pop-culture toys and action figures to collectors, and Woot Bear on Haight Street carries designer toys.
The Caltrain Peninsula line has several publicly accessible spots for watching and photographing trains, per Bay Area railfan guides.
